title: perf(canary): improve auto-detection sensitivity and add rollout hysteresis guards
author: Priya Rao
description: Motivation: Canary pipeline produced noisy regressions during transient load spikes. This PR improves automated detection sensitivity and adds hysteresis-based rollout guards to prevent premature rollbacks or roll-forwards during short-lived variance. Changes include: adaptive thresholds computed from short-term baseline and long-term baseline; KV-cache-aware latency bucketing so cached vs uncached tails are handled separately; hysteresis window and stability counters for canary pass/fail decisions; integration hooks with the rollout controller to gate traffic shifts and automatic rollback with cooldown; telemetry and alerting improvements (deltas, sample counts). Implementation notes: the detector now maintains two rolling windows (short/long), computes dynamic thresholds by percentile + stdev scaling, and requires N consecutive windows over threshold before tripping. The rollout guard accepts 'max-flap' tolerances and enforces cooldowns. Backwards compatibility: existing canary configs are honored; new fields are optional. Migration: migration script adds default hysteresis params to existing canaries. Testing: unit tests for detector, e2e perf canary integration tests, canary simulation harness with historical traces, manual smoke test in staging with synthetic noise. Rollout: merged to main and will roll out to canary controller in the next deploy; operational playbook updated. See files changed for details.

release_notes: Performance canaries: Introduce adaptive threshold detection and hysteresis-based rollout guards to reduce noisy regressions and prevent premature rollbacks. New optional canary config fields: short_window_seconds, long_window_seconds, consecutive_windows_required, cooldown_seconds. Migration script adds conservative defaults. No breaking changes.
